scope: Independent bounded source audit of Claude findings 1, 2, 3, 5, 6. This is evidence, not a production fix, a Lean refinement proof, or a claim that whole CI passes modified production code.

findings.assessment: Shared all-starts budget and timeout retirement supported. Exact claimed default-deployment 12 slow-draft outage not independently reproduced; no raw drafts/timing/timeout settings supplied.
findings.witness: results.json:restart: 12 immediate mocked timeouts at fixed time leave zero workers and block both lanes' normal requests; advancing clock to 60 permits recovery.
caveats: Default feedback timeout is 12 seconds and feedback concurrency is two. Twelve sequential default-duration timeouts span over a minute; even continuous two-worker 12-second timeouts yield roughly 10 feedback starts per 60-second rolling window. The fixed-clock mock does not establish reachability by this real workload.

Canonical mode has input/frame bytes, pool count, per-worker heap and parser-storage limits. The missing explicit bound is cumulative canonical normalization/mapping/distance/trace work, not all limits whatsoever.

Public draft bytes are capped at 8192 (server.py:36,396); JSON request bytes at 16384; Java input/frame limit is 1048576; reference count limit is 4096; owned parser source storage is 67108864 bytes (WorkerSafety.java:45).
No workload that deliberately consumes real CPU, worker capacity or restart budget was run. No canonical expensive-input witness is claimed.
patchContract: Charge work before every potentially expensive phase, including normalization, binder search, every candidate and trace generation. A guard after prepare cannot bound prepare itself.

Retain aggregate launch-rate and process ownership bounds even if startup-failure circuit accounting is separated from request timeout accounting. Counted failed starts alone permits unlimited successful launch/timeout/reap churn; results.json contains a 13-launch/one-window pure countermodel with concurrency one.
Preserve complete pool evaluation and first-minimum ties for accepted workloads; exceeding any shared request budget yields unsupported without publishing partial comparison.

findings.assessment: Supported conditional on documented proxy path: 32 editing channels are per TCP peer, IIS forwards to loopback, and feedback awaits channel allocation.
findings.witness: results.json:channels: 32 loopback allocations succeed, 33rd fails at synthetic times 0 and 899; different peer succeeds; time 900 frees idle slots.
caveats: Channels are allocated lazily on feedback, not automatically for every page/tab that merely opens.
Idle TTL is 900 seconds since seen; active observe calls renew it. Global channel cap remains 512.
A trusted proxy must remove/overwrite untrusted forwarding values and use a documented single-hop or trusted-chain interpretation. Blindly taking XFF permits spoofed quota keys.
HTTP ingress admission happens before request headers are parsed and separately keys client_address[0]; fixing Handler channel identity does not fix ingress per-peer rate aggregation.
patchContract: Only configured trusted proxy peers may contribute a strictly parsed client identity; untrusted/malformed forwarding metadata cannot select a fresh arbitrary quota identity.
Fallback must omit the channel JSON key; explicitly sending channel:null is rejected by server.py:950.
Channel-less requests retain local revision/selection/body/metric/abort guards; they cannot promise channel supersession/cancellation because Scheduler.current(None, revision) is always true.

findings.assessment: Narrow automatic-staleness coverage gap supported. Existing VERIFIED claims are explicitly historical/frozen, and full closure gate already checks all registered hashes.
findings.witness: results.json:staleBridge: mutate only scratch engine_workers.py maxlen 12 to 13; frozen source hash differs while strict_ingress_bridge.check still returns PASS.
caveats: Bridge-only witness does not prove arbitrary engine_workers.py/luna.py/admin_auth.py edits pass the entire CI suite; regression tests may detect behavior changes.
The source manifest contains the source closure; the final evidence manifest additionally contains verifier/proof inputs, so their entry counts differ.

README says VERIFIED at recorded source roots and source-bound report. Documentation also says historical closure never establishes a newer deployed build is verified. A proposed staleness gate must retain this distinction.
patchContract: Current verification requires complete frozen-manifest equality plus bound verifier/evidence identity; any missing or changed required input yields stale/unbound, without changing historical result.
Do not allow a candidate manifest to self-attest a changed file; compare against an independently frozen registered manifest.

findings.assessment: Unconditional health response and unexported uncertainty count supported; 'logging is off' requires qualification.
findings.witness: results.json:health: extracted production public/control health branches both return identical 200 ok for zero versus two mocked feedback workers. Actual reaper retains one synthetic uncertain owner permanently and does not re-probe it.
caveats: Access logs are disabled, but handle_error emits a fixed privacy-preserving stderr diagnostic. Operators are not wholly without any error signal.

Zero idle workers alone is not an outage: startup is lazy and available launch credit may recover capacity. Readiness needs stopped/busy/starting/unreaped/restart-credit context and cannot promise progress from counts alone.

Uncertain-owner retention is an intentional safety decision in the frozen proof, not a justified target for forced release. Admission active count includes retained reservations, but no dedicated uncertain count is returned.
patchContract: Keep public health/liveness semantics explicit and export bounded aggregate diagnostic projections on the loopback control listener only.
Projection excludes learner source, oracle contents, tokens, peer addresses and credentials. Include uncertainty and worker/circuit/lane state without releasing uncertain ownership.
Use a consistent snapshot or expose sample epoch; separate component locks can produce a composite observation that never existed atomically.

findings.assessment: Global failed-login interference supported for enabled and externally reachable HTTPS administration; actual deployment exposure was not inspected.
findings.witness: results.json:admin: production bootstrap/CSRF/authorize accepts two synthetic HTTPS peers; five wrong attempts from one yield five 401 responses; valid password for other principal gets 429 until synthetic time 60.
caveats: Administration is disabled without private configuration. HTTP administration additionally requires loopback, so external availability is conditional, not universal.
CSRF/origin checks protect browser behavior, but a non-browser client can supply Origin and obtain its own preauth cookie/token; those are not proof of trusted operator identity.
Existing authenticated sessions are not revoked merely by filling the failed-login list. The demonstrated denial concerns new sign-in.
patchContract: Restrict the administrative route at an independently enforced deployment boundary or require a trusted operator admission capability before charging its protected login budget.
Per-source buckets alone still need a bounded aggregate KDF/concurrency envelope and do not give liveness against distributed sources or shared NAT without additional assumptions.
A proxy configuration model is conditional evidence; actual IIS enforcement and any bypass listener must be independently checked before claiming deployment closure.
